sections.overview: The Flag Cichlid is a South American freshwater fish in the cichlid family.
sections.identification: Its laterally compressed body bears a bold dark diagonal stripe running from the snout through the eye toward the dorsal fin, which gives it the flag-fish name.
sections.habitat: It inhabits shallow, slow or still freshwater with abundant aquatic plants and sandy or muddy bottoms in the Amazon and Paraguay basins.
sections.diet: A field guide to Bolivian fishes describes it as mainly herbivorous, eating algae, seeds and fruits, with occasional aquatic invertebrates.
sections.behavior: Both parents care for the young; a Bolivian guide also notes that adults may be aggressive in aquariums.
sections.reproduction: In Bolivia, breeding is reported to begin with rising water, and both parents guard the offspring.
sections.ecology: It is a small, plant-associated cichlid of the Amazon and Paraguay drainages; the same genus contains other species, including M. insignis, so genus-level similarities should not be mistaken for identical ranges.
sections.conservation: FishBase reports a global IUCN assessment of Least Concern, dated 20 November 2020.
